oneLiner: The AI buildout's industrial arm: a record $20.5B quarter, a $72B backlog nearly doubled YoY on data-center power demand, and 21.9% adjusted margins - now priced above 30x forward earnings for what history says is a cyclical.
thesis: AI power demand turned Caterpillar's steadiest segment into its growth engine. In Q2 2026 (reported Aug 4), power generation sales rose 29% - sales to users up 72% - on data-center gensets and turbines, and backlog hit a record $72B, up 92% YoY.

The first $20B quarter in company history, with record profitability. Q2 2026 revenue of $20.5B rose 24% on $3.1B of volume and $595M of price; adjusted EPS of $8.17 beat consensus by roughly $1.98 and adjusted operating margin expanded 430bp to 21.9%.

All three primary segments are firing, not just the AI story. Construction Industries grew 35% to $8.35B on North American infrastructure and rental fleet loading, Resource Industries 20% to $4.65B on mining re-equipment, and Power & Energy 17% to roughly $8.2B.

Tariffs are a contained, quantified headwind. Management narrowed the 2026 net tariff cost to about $2.2B (from $2.2-2.6B) on Aug 4, and price realization plus volume more than absorbed it - though Construction margins still took a 340bp hit in Q2.

The cyclical question is the whole debate. At 30x+ forward earnings versus a historical mid-teens multiple, the market is treating the $72B backlog as a multi-year power annuity; only 59% of it ships within 12 months, which is either visibility or hostage-to-AI-capex risk.

latestProse: Caterpillar's Q2 2026 was the first $20 billion quarter in company history: sales of $20.5B rose 24% on $3.1B of volume and $595M of price. Adjusted EPS of $8.17 beat consensus by about $1.98, and adjusted operating margin expanded 430bp to 21.9%. Construction Industries grew 35% to $8.3B, Resource Industries 20% to $4.6B, and Power & Energy 17% to roughly $8.2B, with power generation up 29% on data-center demand. Enterprise operating cash flow was $4.4B, and $2.2B went to buybacks and dividends. The disclosure that matters most: backlog jumped $9B sequentially to a record $72B, up 92% YoY - and only 59% of it ships within 12 months, meaning customers are reserving multi-year power capacity into 2027-28, which is either unprecedented visibility or unprecedented exposure to a single capex theme.
guidanceProse: Management raised full-year 2026 sales and revenue growth to the mid-to-high teens, above its April view, implying roughly $78-80B against 2025's $67.6B. Services revenue is now expected to grow faster than previously guided, and capex holds at $3.5B to fund capacity expansion in large engines and turbines. The tariff estimate narrowed to roughly $2.2B for 2026 (from $2.2-2.6B), with Q2 segment margin impacts of 340bp in Construction Industries, 260bp in Resource Industries, and 90bp in Power & Energy. One flagged headwind: a more typical Construction Industries dealer inventory drawdown of over $1B is expected in Q4, after a $400M build in Q2.

guide.label: FY2026 sales growth guide
guide.sub: Raised Aug 4 from April view; tariff cost narrowed to ~$2.2B; capex held at $3.5B

segments: Power & Energy (formerly Energy & Transportation): ~$8.2B in Q2 2026, +17% YoY, roughly 40% of segment sales - power generation +29% and sales to users +72% on data-center gensets and Solar Turbines
Construction Industries: $8.35B, +35% YoY, roughly 41% - North American infrastructure and dealer rental fleet loading; dealer inventory +$400M in Q2
Resource Industries: $4.65B, +20% YoY, roughly 23% - mining re-equipment demand, copper-led
Financial Products: roughly $1B of quarterly revenues (unverified exact), financing dealer and customer purchases
competitive: Cummins (CMI): the closest fight in data-center power - both are effectively sold out on large gensets; CAT's breadth across reciprocating engines plus Solar Turbines is the differentiator
Deere (DE): different end-market mix (ag-heavy) in a softer 2026 cycle; the divergence in multiples is the market paying for CAT's power exposure
Honeywell (HON): quality-industrial peer on capital allocation and multiple, not products; its portfolio breakup contrasts with CAT's integrated dealer-and-iron model
Komatsu: the global number two in construction and mining equipment; competes on price and currency, not on power generation scale
Generac, Rolls-Royce (mtu), Wartsila: power rivals chasing the same data-center backlog, none with CAT's installed-base services annuity
moat: The dealer network is the moat: the largest independent global dealer organization locks in parts, service, and financing over a machine population measured in decades, turning services into an annuity on installed iron. In power, Caterpillar's large-engine and turbine manufacturing base plus a multi-year backlog form a capacity moat rivals cannot quickly replicate; tariffs, ironically, raise the cost of any challenger importing against it.
risks: Order-cycle reversal: the 92% YoY backlog surge is concentrated in one theme - if hyperscaler capex pauses, backlog math runs in reverse via pushouts and cancellations
Valuation: 30x+ forward earnings on record 21.9% margins is double the historical cyclical multiple; both the E and the multiple can compress together
Tariffs: ~$2.2B net cost in 2026 with Construction margins hit 340bp in Q2; policy remains volatile and price offsets may not repeat in a softer demand tape
Dealer inventory: the Q2 $400M Construction build flatters wholesale versus retail; management already guides a >$1B Q4 destock
Capacity expansion into a possible peak: $3.5B capex and multi-year large-engine expansion create absorption risk if 2027-28 demand disappoints
Macro cyclicality: China construction remains weak, mining capex follows commodity prices, and high rates still gate broader non-residential construction
catalysts: Late Oct 2026 (expected): Q3 2026 earnings - backlog conversion rate and any order-rate deceleration are the tell
Q4 2026: guided Construction Industries dealer destock of over $1B tests underlying retail demand
Oct-Nov 2026: hyperscaler capex updates from MSFT, META, GOOGL, AMZN quarterly prints - the demand signal for the power backlog
Late Jan 2027 (expected): FY2026 results and initial 2027 guidance - first read on whether mid-to-high-teens growth annualizes
pricedIn: At roughly $838 (Aug 10, 2026), CAT is up more than 60% YTD and trades above 30x forward earnings - about double its historical mid-teens cyclical multiple - even after July's pullback from the June 30 all-time high near $1,063. The market is pricing the $72B backlog as a durable, multi-year power annuity: data-center gensets and turbines as structural growth rather than a cycle. What is not priced: order digestion. If AI capex pauses, the 92% YoY order surge becomes pushouts and cancellations, and a 30x multiple on 21.9% peak margins compresses on both axes. The 9-10% post-earnings jump on Aug 4 says the market currently believes the annuity interpretation.

scenarios.bear: Data-center power orders pause in 2027 as hyperscaler capex digests; backlog converts, then shrinks, and part of the 92% order surge cancels. Construction rolls over as the guided Q4 dealer destock (over $1B) extends into 2027, tariffs stay a $2B+ annual cost, and adjusted margins fall from 21.9% toward the mid-teens. EPS declines and the multiple compresses from 30x+ toward the historical mid-to-high teens - a classic late-cycle industrial de-rating.
scenarios.base: The $72B backlog converts steadily through 2027-28: FY26 sales grow mid-to-high teens to roughly $78-80B, then moderate to mid-single digits as power generation stays tight and construction normalizes. Adjusted margins hold near 20% as price offsets roughly $2.2B of tariffs, services compound faster than equipment, capex stays at $3.5B, and buybacks continue. The stock grinds with earnings while the multiple settles toward the mid-20s.
scenarios.bull: Grid scarcity persists into the 2030s and Power & Energy becomes a structural growth franchise: large-engine and turbine capacity expansions sell out years forward, power generation compounds 20%+ off the current base, and backlog keeps setting records. Mining re-equips on copper demand while U.S. infrastructure supports construction. Margins hold above 21% at scale, EPS compounds mid-teens, and the market keeps paying 30x+ for the AI trade's indispensable industrial arm.

valPresets.note: Base-year FCF is cyclically elevated (record margins, backlog conversion), so presets are deliberately modest and fade to a 2.5% terminal. Bear models a post-boom FCF decline, base a GDP-plus glide, bull a sustained power-scarcity ramp. At 30x+ forward, the reverse DCF asks how much of the $72B backlog must annuitize to justify the price.
